title: thornbury peatmoor preclosing compliance exposure
instruction:
You’re the director of ambulatory operations at Thornbury Studios, supporting its purchase of the Texas endoscopy center operated by Peatmoor Solutions. Solveig Sinclair needs a decision-ready compliance view before deal counsel drafts the representation-and-warranty schedules this Friday, and closing is three weeks away. The data room is about 600 pages of payer contracts, Texas facility and federal laboratory records, three years of anesthesia staffing agreements, an old OIG audit letter, and provider files, but she does not want a diligence index or a generic list of everything that might be wrong. She wants only the exposures that could reasonably change the price, become a closing condition, or require a specific representation, warranty, indemnity, or escrow. Prepare the work as of March 1, 2025, applying the requirements relevant to a Texas ambulatory surgery center and its federal program participation. The summary will go to non-specialist investment committee members as well as counsel, so it must be understandable without assuming healthcare-compliance vocabulary.

There are several tensions you need to resolve rather than simply repeat. The anesthesia group has not documented exclusion screening for its clinicians during the last nine months, although its administrator says an annual contractual attestation is sufficient. The operations team regards this as inexpensive housekeeping, while counsel is concerned about services already billed. The compliance vice president also says a confirmed exclusion match is too unlikely to deserve treatment separate from ordinary screening remediation. State counsel has flagged that the current Texas facility license is issued to the seller and will not automatically transfer on the change of ownership, but the integration plan assumes uninterrupted operations from the first morning after closing. Several payer agreements cover 42% of projected cases and contain change-of-control, assignment, or notice language that has not yet been resolved. The seller points to a seven-year-old OIG audit closure letter as evidence that no historical compliance representation is needed. There is also a CLIA certificate for the center’s limited laboratory testing, aging credentialing material in some provider files, and no consolidated account of what happens to Medicare enrollment, accreditation, or payer participation at closing.

Please produce two files: (1) `preclosing_compliance_exposure_summary.docx`, limited to one page, that prioritizes the deal-relevant exposures, states what deal protection each one warrants, and makes clear what is known versus what still needs confirmation; and (2) `deal_exposure_forecast.xlsx`, an editable 90-day estimate showing Base, Expected, and Downside scenarios. For the forecast, use 1,100 planned cases spread evenly across the 90 days, contribution margin of $640 per case, an $18,000 exclusion-screening remediation cost in every scenario, and license-delay assumptions of 0, 30, and 60 days respectively. Pair those with payer-consent lags of 0, 45, and 90 days measured from the first day the center is legally open. During an open day while consent is pending, apply the payer issue only to the 42% affected case volume and model a 55% reduction in contribution margin for those cases. Do not assign assumed dollar values to repayments, penalties, legal fees, or settlement exposure where the necessary claims facts are unavailable; identify that uncertainty without manufacturing precision.

The two files must agree on every figure they share, including the 90-day scenario exposure quoted for decision-making. Keep the Word document to the material call, not background education, and make the spreadsheet transparent enough that Oona Voskresensky can change an assumption without rebuilding it. Write both files into the top level of the working directory you start in, using exactly the filenames above.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `preclosing_compliance_exposure_summary.docx` — One-page, plain-language pre-closing summary of compliance exposures material to price, closing conditions, or agreement protections. (Must be no more than one rendered page, be current as of March 1, 2025, address the Texas transaction, distinguish known facts from unresolved matters, and use exactly the specified filename at the top level of the working directory.)
- `deal_exposure_forecast.xlsx` — Editable 90-day Base, Expected, and Downside estimate of the identified operational compliance exposures. (Must use editable assumptions and formulas, must not assign unsupported values to repayments, penalties, legal fees, or settlements, must agree with every shared figure in the Word summary, and must use exactly the specified filename at the top level of the working directory.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
THORNBURY STUDIOS | PRE-CLOSING COMPLIANCE EXPOSURE
Texas endoscopy center acquisition — decision brief as of March 1, 2025
Priority / status
Known vs. confirm
Deal consequence
Protection, owner & timing
1 • STOP/GO
License
KNOWN: Texas facility license is in seller name and does not automatically transfer on change of ownership. OPEN: buyer application/authorization effective date; separate CLIA update, accreditation and Medicare ASC enrollment/supplier filing.
Without effective buyer authority, closing does not make operations lawful; closed days lose planned contribution margin.
Closing condition: effective license or written regulator authorization. Licensing counsel owns now; operations keeps center closed or delays closing. Confirm CLIA, Medicare and accreditor separately.
2 • HIGH
Payers
KNOWN: unresolved assignment/change-of-control/notice language affects 42% of projected cases. OPEN: contract-specific consent, rates and effective dates.
Participation or rates may not continue; while consent is pending, affected cases carry a modeled 55% contribution-margin reduction. Modeled 90-day total: Base $18,000; Expected $333,979; Downside $541,541.
Payer contracting + counsel obtain consents/amendments before closing; condition or escrow for unresolved material payers. Finance updates forecast; no assumed repayment, penalty or legal-fee dollars.
3 • HIGH
Anesthesia
KNOWN: no documented exclusion screening for contracted clinicians for nine months. Annual vendor attestation is not a substitute for current checks or ongoing monitoring. OPEN: any excluded person and affected claims/payments.
Excluded-person services can threaten billing, program participation and contracts; this is more than housekeeping. A confirmed match is a distinct severe event.
Compliance screens group, entities and personnel against OIG LEIE, SAM and Texas Medicaid source before close and monthly thereafter; seller/anesthesia vendor certifies and buyer retains evidence/audit rights. Match: verify, suspend affected duties/billing, look back dates/services/claims/payments, then counsel-led disclosure/repayment review. Schedule exclusion/billing reps, indemnity/escrow and vendor cure/termination rights.
4 • MEDIUM
History/files
KNOWN: seven-year-old OIG audit closure letter; aging credential files. OPEN: audit scope, corrective-action/refund/reporting/continuing duties; current licenses, privileges, recredentialing and payer enrollment.
Old closure is not blanket proof of current compliance or no unrelated exposure; each provider prerequisite must be current before furnishing or billing.
Deal counsel confirms scope/closure evidence; compliance/medical staff verifies providers and payer enrollment before close. Targeted reps: material compliance, licenses/participation, exclusions, billing/overpayments, investigations and data-room accuracy; indemnity/escrow for identified unknowns.
Decision requested this week: authorize counsel to draft targeted representations, a licensing closing condition, and risk-based indemnity/escrow; require the owners above to deliver confirmations before Friday schedule drafting. Forecast excludes unquantified repayments, penalties, settlements and legal fees pending facts.

spec.professional_context: Thornbury Studios is preparing to acquire a Texas endoscopy center from Peatmoor Solutions. The director of ambulatory operations must convert fragmented healthcare-compliance concerns into a concise deal-protection summary and a defensible short-term financial estimate for non-specialist decision makers.
difficulty_sources: Materiality triage across overlapping healthcare licensing, exclusion-screening, payer, enrollment, credentialing, and transaction concerns
Distinguishing confirmed deficiencies from contingent liabilities without understating deal risk
Resolving overlap between operational shutdown loss and payer-participation impairment in a 90-day scenario model
Compressing actionable deal protections, owners, timing, uncertainty, and financial consequences into one page
Maintaining exact numerical and terminological consistency across a narrative document and an editable workbook

authoring_plan.mode_intent: Create a normative one-page deal document whose quality depends on a healthcare operations manager knowing which compliance matters can affect lawful operation, historical billing exposure, revenue continuity, and contractual risk allocation. Pair it with a formula-driven estimate that translates supplied operating assumptions into deal-relevant scenarios.
imperfections_and_tensions_to_preserve: Contracted anesthesia personnel have a nine-month exclusion-screening documentation lapse, while the vendor relies on annual attestation. The gold must reject attestation or annual review as an adequate replacement for current and ongoing screening.

A confirmed exclusion match is unlikely but severe. The gold must treat it as a distinct escalation path involving verification, immediate restriction from affected work or billing, a service-and-claims lookback, and fact-based disclosure or repayment analysis.

The state facility license belongs to the seller and does not automatically transfer. The gold must not permit operation after closing without effective buyer authority and should make licensure a closing condition with a lawful contingency.
Payer contracts affecting 42% of cases contain unresolved assignment, change-of-control, notice, or consent language. The gold must avoid assuming uniform continuity.
An old federal audit closure letter has limited scope and age. The gold must not treat it as blanket proof of current compliance or absence of unrelated historical liabilities.

Laboratory certification, state facility licensure, Medicare enrollment or supplier status, accreditation, provider credentials, and payer enrollment are separate dependencies and must not be collapsed into one approval.

The financial estimate lacks facts needed to value repayments, penalties, settlements, or legal fees. Those categories remain explicitly unquantified rather than assigned zero as a substantive conclusion.

gold_relationships.daily_planned_cases: Planned case volume divided by the 90-day horizon.
gold_relationships.license_delay_loss: Planned cases multiplied by license-delay days divided by 90, then multiplied by contribution margin per case.
gold_relationships.open_days: The greater of zero and 90 minus license-delay days.
gold_relationships.payer_affected_days: The lesser of payer-consent lag and open days because payer impairment begins only when legal operation begins and cannot affect cases already lost to closure.
gold_relationships.payer_consent_loss: Daily planned cases multiplied by payer-affected days, affected payer share, contribution-margin reduction percentage, and contribution margin per case.
gold_relationships.scenario_total: License-delay loss plus payer-consent loss plus one screening-remediation cost.
gold_relationships.base_inputs: Zero license-delay days and zero payer-consent-lag days.
gold_relationships.expected_inputs: Thirty license-delay days and forty-five payer-consent-lag days.
gold_relationships.downside_inputs: Sixty license-delay days and ninety payer-consent-lag days, capped to the thirty open days remaining in the horizon.
gold_relationships.cross_file_rule: Any workbook output quoted in the one-page summary must match the workbook, allowing only transparent whole-dollar rounding.

professional_content_expected: Deal materiality triage tied to economics, conditions precedent, and targeted agreement protections.
Current and monthly exclusion screening of relevant individuals and entities using federal and applicable state sources, with buyer verification over delegated screening.
Separate response for a credible or confirmed exclusion match, including immediate control, retrospective claims review, and counsel-guided reporting or repayment assessment.
Facility licensure as a prerequisite to operation and a closing condition, with a lawful delay contingency.
Separate treatment of laboratory certification, Medicare enrollment or supplier continuity, accreditation, payer contracting, and provider credentialing.
Contract-specific payer consent analysis and a quantified revenue effect based only on the supplied assumptions.
Limited reliance on historical audit closure documentation and confirmation of scope, corrective actions, refunds, reporting, and continuing obligations.
Specific representations, warranties, indemnity or escrow concepts, accountable functions, and timing.
Plain-language explanations suitable for non-specialists and calibrated statements of uncertainty.
workbook_behavior: Inputs must be editable numeric cells and scenario outputs must be formula-driven.
The model must prevent overlap between cases lost during license closure and cases financially impaired while open but awaiting payer consent.
The supplied remediation cost is included exactly once in every scenario.
Unsupported contingent liabilities are excluded from quantified totals with an explicit explanation that they remain unquantified pending facts.
A test edit to a major assumption must propagate through all affected outputs.
authoring_plan.intended_verdict: A passing reference solution fits on one rendered Word page, identifies the small set of compliance matters that can alter the transaction, actively corrects the annual-attestation misuse, isolates the severe exclusion-match exception, makes lawful operation contingent on effective licensing, and provides a transparent three-scenario workbook whose values reconcile exactly with the summary.

deliverables.description: One-page, plain-language pre-closing summary of compliance exposures material to price, closing conditions, or agreement protections.
constraints: Must be no more than one rendered page, be current as of March 1, 2025, address the Texas transaction, distinguish known facts from unresolved matters, and use exactly the specified filename at the top level of the working directory.

deliverables.description: Editable 90-day Base, Expected, and Downside estimate of the identified operational compliance exposures.
constraints: Must use editable assumptions and formulas, must not assign unsupported values to repayments, penalties, legal fees, or settlements, must agree with every shared figure in the Word summary, and must use exactly the specified filename at the top level of the working directory.
